subsystems.name: Feedstock store
subsystems.role: holds refined food ingredients — protein, fat, carbohydrate, vitamins and minerals — in stable, food-grade form.
parts: refrigerated compartments for oils and emulsions

subsystems.name: Deposition head
subsystems.role: places each ingredient precisely, in layers or droplets, under software control.

subsystems.name: Structuring module
subsystems.role: gives the deposited mass the fibrous, layered or aerated texture that makes it read as food.

subsystems.name: Cooking and setting stage
subsystems.role: applies heat, cold or enzymes to cook and fix the printed portion.

subsystems.name: Personalisation controller
subsystems.role: turns a person's dietary targets and health measurements into a recipe and a print file.
parts: input for blood-marker or body-composition data

subsystems.name: Hygiene system
subsystems.role: keeps a warm, nutrient-rich machine free of microbial growth between meals.

buildSteps.title: Produce the ingredients
buildSteps.detail: Purified proteins, fats, carbohydrates, vitamins and minerals are made by precision fermentation, enzymatic conversion, extraction and chemical synthesis, then dried or pasteurised into stable food-grade powders and pastes. Note that a machine cannot build food atom by atom: food chemistry happens in bulk reactors, not by mechanical placement of molecules, so the appliance is an assembler of refined ingredients.

buildSteps.title: Formulate printable inks
buildSteps.detail: Each ingredient is blended with water, edible binders and gelling agents so it flows through a nozzle, then holds shape once deposited.

buildSteps.title: Build the deposition head
buildSteps.detail: Separate channels, metering pumps and nozzles are provided for each ingredient class, so protein, fat, carbohydrate and micronutrients can be laid down independently and in controlled ratios.

buildSteps.title: Print the structure
buildSteps.detail: Layer order, line width and nozzle path are programmed to create texture rather than a uniform block: aligned fibres, thin layers, hollow cells and gel pockets that mimic the mouthfeel of meat, bread or fruit.

buildSteps.title: Set and cook the portion
buildSteps.detail: The printed item is heated, chilled or treated with enzymes so proteins set, starches gelatinise and the structure becomes stable and safe to eat.

buildSteps.title: Sense and correct
buildSteps.detail: Cameras and flow sensors check layer quality and mass, and the controller adjusts the print in real time.

buildSteps.title: Personalise the recipe
buildSteps.detail: Dietary targets, allergies and measured health markers select the ingredient ratios and added micronutrients for that individual.

buildSteps.title: Clean and sterilise
buildSteps.detail: The machine flushes and sanitises its own food paths after each meal, since warm nutrient residues are an ideal growth medium for microbes.

prerequisites.tech: Precision fermentation of food proteins and fats
prerequisites.why: it already makes enzymes and some proteins at food grade, but most protein and fat in diets is still farmed.
printers that extrude single pastes such as chocolate, dough or purée exist, but multi-material meals are not demonstrated.
the processed-food industry already uses these to rebuild texture, and a fabricator would depend on them heavily.

prerequisites.tech: Predictive models of how structure creates taste and texture
prerequisites.why: without these, a machine cannot know which printed geometry will actually taste and chew like the food it replaces.

prerequisites.tech: Cheap, continuous nutrition and health sensing
prerequisites.why: some markers can be measured today, but a validated model that converts them into an optimal meal does not exist.

pathway.milestone: single-material food printers in labs and restaurants, and precision-fermented proteins sold as ingredients
pathway.unlocks: proof that food can be deposited and cooked under digital control.

pathway.milestone: multi-material printers that combine protein, fat and carbohydrate with binders into simple foods such as patties or bars
pathway.unlocks: appliances that make a recognisable food item, not just a garnish.

pathway.milestone: closed-loop personalisation, where measured health markers and gut-microbiome data set the recipe
pathway.unlocks: nutrition genuinely tailored to an individual rather than to an average.

pathway.milestone: cheap synthesis of more building blocks from simple feedstocks such as sugars, methanol or hydrogen and captured carbon dioxide
pathway.unlocks: staple foods made without farming, if texture, energy use and cost can be brought under control.
